text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-The government wants to become a large investor in foreign companies. The aim is to increase Norwegian competitiveness and secure long-term ownership.

-People have great expectations of the government's long-term programme, which is due to be presented on Friday. Four years ago the outlook was pessimistic, but thanks to the oil industry wages have increased and interest rates have fallen.

-Consultancy firm Mckinsey & Co sees a considerable need for restructuring in the Nordic finance sector. Fokus Bank, Nordlandsbanken and a series of small saving banks are likely to be bought by larger institutions, McKinsey says.
-Industrial holding company Aker RGI has sold 35 percent of its stake in real estate company Avantor for about 550 million crowns. The sale is part of a strategy to concentrate on its core business.

-It is crucial that final approval for the two planned natural gas power plants is given by the summer. Auke Lont, managing director at Naturkraft -- the company set up to build and operate the plants, says postponing the decision will make it impossible to fulfil signed contracts.
